subject: [hw] V33 finding in n2fmt: zero-flag width > ~480 overflows char body[480]
body:
While exercising V33-s stdio bridge I hit an ASan/UBSan failure inside shim/n2shim_format.c (not my file, not fixed by me):

  shim/n2shim_format.c:670:3: runtime error: index 480 out of bounds for type char[480]
  (or :672 for a slightly different width)

Repro (clang -std=c11 -O1 -g -fsanitize=address,undefined -fno-sanitize-recover=all, real n2a32_mem, one cpu, c.r[0]=1):
  n2fmt(c, buf, 1<<20, guest("%0600d"), args)  -> overflow at line 670
  n2fmt(..., "%0481d", ...)                    -> overflow at line 672
  "%0600x" "%0600o" "%0600u"                   -> same as %0600d
  "%0600f" not tested (needs a double arg)
Not affected: "%600d" (space pad), "%-600d", "%0600c", "%600.500d" (all 600 chars, no UB).

Cause: emit_int() materialises the zero padding into char body[PREC_MAX + 80] (= 480 bytes) at lines 666-672 (`for (i=0;i<zeros;i++) body[np+i] = 0`), while zeros can be width - np - nd up to the clamped width (999999999). Space padding goes through opad() and is O(1); the zero path is not. Threshold: width > sizeof(body) - np - nd, so about 479-480 for a 1-digit value, earlier with a longer digit string.

Suggested fix: do not materialise zero padding; if np+zeros+nd > sizeof body, emit prefix, then opad(o, 0, zeros), then digits via oputn (emit_field already has this shape for the zero case when width > blen; the overflow is only in building body). Or cap zeros at sizeof(body)-np-nd for the body copy and let emit_field add the rest.

Note: this is reachable from the guest: any guest format with the 0 flag and a width above ~480 (e.g. a debug dump written as %0512d). It is not reachable from the vendor set as far as I know (I did not census its format strings), so it is not a blocker, but V33-s test found it under the mandated sanitizers.

My test no longer exercises it (I switched my heap-path test to a 600-byte %s). V33 STATUS records the finding and points here. Please post DONE V30 rev N when fixed and I will re-run my suite.
